thread:
rina: Quick PSA from a customer repro on Pixel emulator (API 33/34): Kotlin SDK + Retrofit + OkHttp 4.11.0 saw duplicate POSTs when token refresh and TLS handshake failures interleave. Slightly different from the usual non-repeatable body problem.
chao: TLS handshake failures? that sounds like a different root. details?
rina: sequence we saw: connection fails mid-request (TLS handshake / SSLException), OkHttp retries the call, Authenticator triggers a refresh on a separate thread, handshake succeeds on retry, but server received two identical POSTs. It only happens with streaming bodies and specific okhttp/conscrypt combos on emulator.
marta: hmm. maybe conscrypt re-negotiation + connection pool reuse leads to a retry path where the request body is re-sent. Can you paste the minimal RequestBody and authenticator pattern?
rina: RequestBody is a small streaming wrapper over an InputStream (non-repeatable). Authenticator is similar to previous examples but we used a custom call that sometimes fails with SSLHandshakeException.
chao: log snippet:
```
12:03:10.001 POST /events -> handshake_failure SSLException
12:03:10.210 Authenticator -> refresh token (uses dedicated client)
12:03:10.460 POST /events -> retry after connection reestablished
12:03:10.485 POST /events -> duplicate payload seen by server
```
chao: notable: we already used a dedicated auth client to avoid dispatcher starvation, so this isn't the blocking-auth case. Instead it's interaction between retryOnConnectionFailure, conscrypt TLS behavior on emulator, and non-repeatable bodies.
marta: ok that is new-ish. Workarounds?
rina: we tested three things: 1) disable retryOnConnectionFailure on uploader client — duplicates stopped; 2) buffer body to a repeatable ByteString/file — duplicates stopped; 3) set request header `Expect: 100-continue` so server can reject before body send (reduced duplicates in some cases).
chao: interesting about Expect header. Example code for disabling retry: ```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .build()
```
rina: and tiny snippet for `Expect: 100-continue` (Retrofit-level request builder):
```kotlin
request.newBuilder()
  .header("Expect", "100-continue")
  .build()
```
marta: Expect helps because client waits for 100 continue before sending body, so if server immediately errors or TLS blows before that you avoid sending body twice. Not perfect but can mitigate.
chao: conscrypt/okhttp versions matter. In our internal matrix we saw the issue on OkHttp 4.11.0 + Conscrypt 2.1.5 on emulator API34, but not on OkHttp 4.10.0. Might be a regression in connection pool handshake retry. Can someone file a minimal repro and open an issue upstream?
rina: opened repro in kotlin-sdk-repros with a small server that simulates handshake failure then accepts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kotlin-sdk-repros/pull/115. CI run queued.
ci-bot: CI build 4822 for branch conscrypt-handshake-repro started: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/4822 :eyes:
marta: doc ask: add a short note in devex: "Emulator TLS + non-repeatable bodies -> duplicates" with recommended mitigations: disable retryOnConnectionFailure for non-repeatable uploads, buffer or use idempotency keys, set Expect: 100-continue when supported, and test OkHttp/Conscrypt combinations. Also include a link to the repro.
chao: I'll draft the doc and add a test matrix entry for okhttp+conscrypt on emulator. Could prevent customer surprises.
rina: thanks! saved an incident. :pray:
